newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power holds steady through to Monday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power holds steady through to Monday.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West held steady Friday with virtually no trade between the Thanksgiving Day holiday and the weekend, industry sources said.
Weather through much of the U.S., with the exception of the East Coast and a large portion of the Southeast, was forecast to be below-normal from December 3 to 7.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm next day power deals for Monday delivery were notionally pegged steady at $25.00-27.00, the sources said.
Round-the-clock power through to the end of the weekend had been talked Wednesday, prior to many traders leaving the office for the holiday weekend, at $14.00-16.00.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were notionally pegged steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Monday was assessed steady at $23.00-25.00 per MWh.
Round-the clock power through to the end of the weekend was assessed at $14.50-16.50 on Wednesday, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Monday delivery were assessed at $22.00-23.00 per MWh.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
December peak ECAR was talked steady at $22.00-23.00, with January/February ECAR was also assessed steady at $23.00-24.00 per MWh.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for Monday were talked steady at $26.00-27.50.
December SPP was assessed steady at $24.00-26.50, while January/February was pegged unchanged at $27.00-27.50 per MWh.
